title: Introduce autoswap batch-cache arbitrator and adaptive quant-tier shim
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an autoswap arbitrator for batch-cache that allows tenant-aware cache slot swaps and an adaptive quantization-tier shim with safety rollback. Backwards compatible. Opt-in behind feature flag 'autoswap_arbitrator'.
description: Motivation: Prefill/cache pressure can produce suboptimal unit economics when cold and hot tenants contend for limited batch-cache slots. This PR implements an 'autoswap' arbitrator that proactively swaps cache ownership based on short-window unit-econ signals and latency SLO risk, plus a lightweight adaptive quant-tier shim that temporarily relaxes quantization aggressiveness for delicate queries to reduce quality regressions. Design summary: 1) arbitrator core (pkg/arbiter) evaluates tenant score vectors (recent tokens-per-second, miss-rate, cost-per-token delta, SLO-violation probability) and proposes swap actions; 2) swap executor applies cache slot handoff with graceful KV-preserve protocol and metrics/events for tracing; 3) quant-tier shim hooks into runtime request path and can escalate or de-escalate quant-tier for a specific request batch to balance latency and loss during a swap window; 4) feature-flag gating and operator-configurable policy weights with safe fallthrough to existing FIFO eviction. This PR is intentionally conservative: autoswap is disabled by default and requires tenant opt-in or operator policy. Checklist: - [x] core arbitrator algorithm and unit tests - [x] integration tests for swap handoff and KV integrity - [x] metrics (swap.proposed, swap.executed, swap.failed, quant_tier.adjusted) - [x] console docs and ops runbook page - [x] helm-chart flag and operator guide - [x] canary rollout plan added Implementation notes: The arbitrator runs as a lightweight controller inside the prefill controller group and uses existing lease-based locking on cache partitions. Swap proposals are ranked and can be filtered by policy (latency-first | econ-first). The quant-tier shim is a middleware inserted at the inference runtime path; it executes a deterministic decision and can attach a temporary quant-hint header to the request so serving workers select the correct kernels. Rollback: feature flag off returns behavior to existing eviction. In the unlikely data-loss path the executor attempts KV duplication to an ephemeral shard and will prefer rollback to previous owner. Performance testing: local bench shows 6-9% unit-cost reduction for mixed workloads with heavy tenant skew on small caches with negligible median latency delta (+1.5ms). Safety: added reduction in swap churn via minimum swap-interval and hysteresis thresholds. Related: ENG-1428 implements metrics schema changes; SUP-981 references a customer incident that motivated tenant-aware swaps. Notes for reviewers: focus on lock ordering in pkg/arbiter/executor.go and on the race between quant-tier shim applying a change and runtime kernel selection. Migration: no DB migrations required, config lives in the existing prefill config map.

operational_runbook: Enable feature flag 'autoswap_arbitrator' in prefills configmap to start canary
Start canary at 5% tenant allocation and monitor swap.executed and swap.failed metrics
If swap.failed > 0.5% or median latency delta > 10ms over 1h window, toggle feature flag off and file an incident
To force a manual swap rollback: POST /admin/prefill/swap/rollback with partition id and previous_owner
Policy tuning knobs: min_swap_interval, econ_weight, latency_weight, max_daily_swaps_per_tenant
notes_for_release_engineers: Feature gated: no auto-enablement in prod clusters
Helm chart bump included: update chart version before deploy
Add metrics to central dashboard: swap.executed, swap.proposed, swap.failed, swap.churn, quant_tier.adjusted
qa_notes: Added targeted QA scenarios: tenant skew synthetic workload, mid-swap runtime failures, and quant-tier quality regression check. QA validated KV-preserve semantics and rollback path. Expected behavior documented in ops page.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: conservative rollout, feature flag off by default. Main risk is swap churn causing increased latency if policy weights are aggressive; mitigations include hysteresis and min-swap-interval. No persistent data schema changes.

synthesized_unit_econ_estimate: Based on canary sims, expected 4-9% unit-cost reduction for 70/30 hot/cold tenant mixes on constrained caches. This depends on policy weights and cache size.
